31	## D6 Mutation testing (new)
32	
33	- Tool: **StrykerJS with the Vitest runner** (Actual Budget). Hand-made mutations don't count.
34	- Pick one issue whose PR changes both source and tests; mutate **only the source files changed by that PR** (535: two issues).
35	- Add `"json"` to Stryker `reporters`. Commit `docs/sprint3/mutation/reports/<issue#>-<username>-before.json` and `-after.json`, plus the config and command. Reusing a teammate's config is fine if credited, but each student runs it themselves.
36	- Analyze every survivor (if more than 10, at least 10, starting with lines the PR changed): **equivalent** or **test gap**, and why.
37	- Add or strengthen at least one test that kills a gap survivor; it must show as killed in the "after" report. Scores quoted in the write-up must match the reports.
38	- Write-up `docs/sprint3/mutation/<issue#>-<username>.md`: title `Mutation testing: Issue #<N> -- <title>`. Header fields: PR(s), Tool, Config (link + credit), Command, Reports (before/after links), Mutation score before% → after%. Surviving mutants table (Location file:line | Mutation | Equivalent or test gap? | Why). New or strengthened test (commit link, file › test name, which mutant it kills). Questions: (1) what survivors revealed about the tests; (2) whether any survivor exposed an assertion whose expected value wasn't based on the requirements; (3) AI use and what was verified or corrected, or N/A.
39	- Rubric: tool run on PR files with config, command, and reports committed 4 · survivors analyzed correctly 4 · a killing test, confirmed by re-run 4 · answers show understanding 3.
40	- Common problems: tests that already fail on unchanged code stop Stryker, so fix or exclude them; tests that run against `dist` never see the mutants; narrowing the test set can produce fake survivors. If blocked, ask teammates first, then the TA early (with the errors and the AI log).

42	Extra credit: an upstream PR accepted or under active review (+3 each); an upstream bug report confirmed by maintainers (+2 each).

## Summary

Follow-up to #120. Add a permanent, manually started GitHub Actions workflow that regenerates the VRT screenshots for a given PR in CI's Playwright container and commits the changed PNGs to that PR's branch. This turns the temporary workflow from #116 into a tool anyone on the team can run.

## Problem/ User Scenario

When a PR changes the UI, its VRT screenshots have to be regenerated in CI's exact environment (`mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.61.1-jammy` on x86_64). Screenshots made in our arm64 dev containers don't match CI, and the dev containers have no Docker. Right now we have no working way to do this:

- **Upstream's `/update-vrt` comment bot doesn't run here.** Every job is limited to `actualbudget/actual` and asks for Depot runners. Teammates have tried it, and every run was skipped: [Oct 30](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/actual-budget/actions/runs/40995490314), [Oct 30](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/actual-budget/actions/runs/40995947533), [Nov 7](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/actual-budget/actions/runs/42389549446).
- **Our "VRT Comment" bot still tells people to comment `/update-vrt`** when VRT fails, which sends them to the broken path.
- **The only working method is manual.** Copy the temporary workflow from #116 into the PR branch, run it, then remember to delete it before merging.

## Goal/ User Story

Anyone on the team can regenerate their PR's screenshots from the Actions tab in one run, without adding a temporary workflow to their PR.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A workflow named "Update VRT screenshots" on `master` can be started from the Actions tab with a PR number as input. It runs on GitHub-hosted runners, in the same Playwright container image and with the same build steps as the CI VRT job.
2. When screenshots differ, the workflow pushes one commit to the PR's branch that changes only `.png` files in `*-snapshots/` folders (`--update-snapshots=changed`). When nothing differs, no commit is pushed, and the run summary says so.
3. After that commit, the PR's VRT job passes when it is re-run.
4. The workflow fails without pushing anything, and with a clear message, when the PR is closed, when its branch is in a different repository, or when the generated changes include any non-PNG file.
5. When VRT fails, the VRT Comment bot points to the new workflow instead of `/update-vrt`. The "CI in our fork" section of `STUDENTS.md` explains how to run the workflow and that VRT has to be re-run afterwards. The Fork CI guard check passes.

## Out of Scope

- Making upstream's `/update-vrt` comment bot work in our fork (see Design).
- Electron desktop VRT screenshots, and Windows/macOS screenshots.
- Changing VRT tolerance settings (`maxDiffPixels: 5`, `threshold: 0.05`).
- Making the E2E/VRT check required on `master`.
- PRs opened from personal forks (all our PRs come from branches in this repo).

## Open Questions

- Should the workflow re-run VRT on the PR itself after pushing? Commits pushed with `GITHUB_TOKEN` don't start CI. The alternatives are a personal access token secret (needs a repo admin) or a re-run by hand.
- Should the workflow regenerate every VRT file, or accept an optional list of test files to keep runs shorter?

## Rough Scope

**Medium (3 points).** One new workflow file in `.github/workflows/`, a one-line text change in `e2e-vrt-comment.yml`, and a `STUDENTS.md` update. No app code changes. Most of the logic already exists in #116's temporary workflow. The work is in making it general (any PR, safety checks for AC 4), testing it on real PRs, and documenting it.

## Source

- Open Questions and Out of Scope of #120, which deferred a permanent workflow (alternative 3 in its Design).
- Tech Debt "Encountered" in PR #116: "A reusable 'Update VRT snapshots' workflow for the fork would avoid repeating this."
- The skipped `/update-vrt` runs linked above.

## Design

**Decision:** Add a new, separate `workflow_dispatch` workflow that takes a PR number, regenerates the screenshots in CI's container, and commits the changed PNGs with `GITHUB_TOKEN`.

**Alternatives considered:**

1. **Adapt upstream's `/update-vrt` workflows** (`vrt-update-generate.yml` and `vrt-update-apply.yml`). Starting it from a PR comment is convenient. Rejected because it means editing two upstream files on every job (the repository guard and the runner labels), which risks merge conflicts at each upstream sync. It also needs an `ACTIONS_UPDATE_TOKEN` secret or a token change, and comment-triggered workflows can only be tested after they're on `master`.
2. **Keep using a temporary workflow per PR** (as in #116). No new files on `master`. Rejected because every UI PR has to repeat the setup, and a temporary workflow can accidentally be merged.

**Rationale:** A new file can't conflict with upstream changes, and the approach has already worked once: #116's temporary workflow made screenshots that matched CI using only `GITHUB_TOKEN`. A manual workflow can also be tried from a branch before merging.

**Consequences:**

- *Easier:* Any teammate can update screenshots in one run, with no Docker or local setup and no cleanup before merging.
- *Harder:* People start it from the Actions tab rather than with a PR comment. VRT still has to be re-run by hand after the bot's commit (unless we add a token). The VRT Comment text edit is a one-line difference from upstream.

## Hardening evidence plan

- Before: the skipped `/update-vrt` runs above, and the manual temporary-workflow process from #116.
- After: links to a successful run on a real UI PR, the commit it pushed, and the VRT run that passed afterwards. Plus a run showing it refusing a non-PNG change (AC 4).

STUDENTS.md
226:## 9. CI in our fork
227-
228-Our GitHub Actions workflows (`.github/workflows/`) come from upstream. Upstream runs them on
229-**Depot**, a paid runner service (`runs-on: depot-ubuntu-latest`). We don't have Depot, so a job
230-that asks for a `depot-*` runner waits in the queue until GitHub cancels it, about 24 hours later
231-(issue #101). Our fork changes that in three ways:
232-
233-- **Checks that run on our PRs use GitHub's free runners** (`ubuntu-latest`). That covers Test
234-  (lint, typecheck, unit tests), Build, E2E and visual regression tests, the API browser test, and
235-  the Linux Electron build. The macOS and Windows builds are turned off.
236-- **Upstream-only workflows are turned off** with `if: github.repository == 'actualbudget/actual'`
237-  on each job. They show as "skipped" here. These are publishing and releases (npm, Docker,
238-  Netlify, Flathub, Microsoft Store, nightly desktop app), the stale-PR closer, autofix.ci, the
239-  release-notes check, `/update-vrt`, the issue bots that point at upstream, and the bot that
240-  labels `[AI]` PRs (we review AI-generated PRs by hand).
241-- **The `Fork CI guard` check** runs `.github/scripts/fork-ci-runners.mjs` on every PR. It fails
242-  if any job that can run here still asks for a Depot runner.
243-
244-**A red check doesn't block merging.** No check is marked "required", so you can merge a PR with
245-a failing check and fix the problem in a later PR. Before you merge, compare the PR's failing
246-checks with `master`'s. If they're the same failures, your PR didn't break anything new.
247-
248-### After merging an upstream release
249-
250-Upstream edits can bring Depot runners back, either in a merge conflict or silently in a new job.
251-
252-1. In a merge conflict on a `runs-on:`/`runner:` line or a guard `if:` line, **keep our version**.
253-2. Run the checker and let it swap any new Linux Depot labels to GitHub's Linux runners:
254-
255-   ```bash
256-   node .github/scripts/fork-ci-runners.mjs --fix
257-   node .github/scripts/fork-ci-runners.mjs   # should print "No unguarded Depot runner labels found."
258-   ```
259-
260-3. If it still reports a **macOS or Windows** label, `--fix` deliberately left it alone, because we
261-   run CI on Linux only. Remove that entry from the job's matrix, or turn off the whole job (step 4).
262-4. If upstream added a new workflow that **publishes or releases** something, don't swap its
263-   runner. Add `if: github.repository == 'actualbudget/actual'` to each of its jobs instead, so it
264-   never runs here.
265-
266-Happy budgeting! 🎉
````

+name: TEMP - Update VRT snapshots
+# TEMPORARY: regenerates stale VRT snapshots in the same environment as the
+# `vrt` job in e2e-test.yml and commits the changed PNGs back to this branch.
+# Remove this file once the snapshots are committed.
+
+on:
+  push:
+    branches:
+      - fix/update-vrt-snapshots
+
+permissions:
+  contents: read
+
+concurrency:
+  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
+  cancel-in-progress: true
+
+env:
+  VRT_FILES: >-
+    e2e/budget.test.ts
+    e2e/command-bar.test.ts
+    e2e/help-menu.test.ts
+    e2e/rules.test.ts
+    e2e/schedules.test.ts
+    e2e/settings.test.ts
+    e2e/transactions.test.ts
+
+jobs:
+  build-web:
+    name: Build web bundle
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@de0fac2e4500dabe0009e67214ff5f5447ce83dd # v6.0.2
+        with:
+          persist-credentials: false
+      - name: Set up environment
+        uses: ./.github/actions/setup
+        with:
+          download-translations: 'false'
+      - name: Build browser bundle
+        env:
+          REACT_APP_NETLIFY: 'true'
+        run: yarn build:browser --skip-translations
+      - name: Upload build artifact
+        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
+        with:
+          name: desktop-client-build
+          path: packages/desktop-client/build/
+          retention-days: 1
+          overwrite: true
+
+  update-vrt:
+    name: Update VRT snapshots
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    needs: build-web
+    permissions:
+      contents: write
+    container:
+      image: mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.61.1-jammy
+    env:
+      E2E_USE_BUILD: '1'
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@de0fac2e4500dabe0009e67214ff5f5447ce83dd # v6.0.2
+      - name: Set up environment
+        uses: ./.github/actions/setup
+        with:
+          download-translations: 'false'
+      - name: Trust the repository directory
+        run: git config --global --add safe.directory "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
+      - name: Download web build
+        uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
+        with:
+          name: desktop-client-build
+          path: packages/desktop-client/build/
+      - name: Regenerate changed snapshots
+        run: yarn vrt --update-snapshots=changed $VRT_FILES
+      - name: Verify regenerated snapshots
+        run: yarn vrt $VRT_FILES
+      - name: Upload snapshots artifact
+        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
+        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
+        with:
+          name: vrt-snapshots
+          path: packages/desktop-client/e2e/*-snapshots/
+          retention-days: 7
+      - name: Commit and push snapshots

+          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
+          git config user.email "github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"

  timeout: 60000, // 60 seconds
  retries: 1,
  fullyParallel: true,
  workers: Number(process.env.E2E_WORKERS) || (process.env.CI ? 4 : undefined),
  testDir: 'e2e/',
  reporter: process.env.CI
    ? [['blob'], ['list'], ['junit', { outputFile: 'test-results/junit.xml' }]]
    : [['html', { open: 'never' }]],

    userAgent: 'playwright',
    screenshot: 'only-on-failure',
    browserName: 'chromium',
    baseURL: process.env.E2E_START_URL ?? `http://localhost:${e2ePort}`,
    trace: 'on-first-retry',
    ignoreHTTPSErrors: true,
  },
  expect: {
    // Default expect timeout (5s) is too tight for initial render of the
    // budget page in the production bundle under CI CPU contention —
    // the budget-table testid lives inside AutoSizer, which returns null
    // until layout provides width/height, and that can take >5s. Bumping
    // to 10s lets those assertions settle without per-test overrides.
    timeout: 10_000,
    // `threshold` is pixelmatch's per-pixel YIQ-delta cutoff — a pixel
    // counts toward `maxDiffPixels` only if its delta exceeds
    // 35215 * threshold². Playwright's 0.2 default lets faint color
    // overlays (e.g. rgba(…, .15) row striping) slip through with 0
    // reported diff pixels; 0.05 catches them while staying above
    // anti-aliasing noise.
    toHaveScreenshot: { maxDiffPixels: 5, threshold: 0.05 },
  },

**Issue #153 AC 3 says VRT passes 'when re-run' after the bot's screenshot commit, but GitHub re-runs test the old commit SHA, and pushes made with GITHUB_TOKEN don't start CI. How should CI run on the bot's commit?**

Options:
- **Auto-dispatch E2E (Recommended)** - Add a `workflow_dispatch` trigger to e2e-test.yml (2 lines in an upstream file). The update workflow then starts E2E on the PR branch itself, so checks appear on the new commit with no manual step. Small merge-conflict risk in the `on:` block at upstream syncs.
- **Manual: empty commit** - No upstream file changes. STUDENTS.md tells people to push an empty commit (or close and reopen the PR) after the bot commits, which starts CI on the new head. Matches the issue's original scope, but I'd post a spec-change comment fixing AC 3's 're-run' wording.

**Issue #153 open question 2: should the workflow accept an optional list of test files (e.g. `e2e/budget.test.ts`) so runs are shorter, or always regenerate every VRT file?**

Options:
- **Optional input (Recommended)** - Blank means all VRT tests across 3 shards like CI. Filled in means only those files. Costs one extra input, validated so it can only contain e2e test paths.
- **Always all files** - Simpler and nothing can be missed, but every run takes the full ~15–20 min.


**Answer:** Auto-dispatch E2E (Recommended), For this, let's do the first option, where blank means all VRT across all 3 shards like CI, filled in means only those files, but our bot response guides the user through how to update the failed screenshots". Read the answers carefully — they may request clarification, changes, or that you not proceed — and follow what they actually say.

```mjs
// Fork-only helper for CSCI-435-SE/actual-budget (issue #153).
//
// Reads the Playwright JUnit reports that the `vrt` job in e2e-test.yml
// uploads (`vrt-junit-*` artifacts) and prints the VRT test files that had a
// failing test, as one space-separated line of `e2e/<file>` paths. The VRT
// Comment bot puts that line in its comment so people can paste it into the
// "Update VRT screenshots" workflow's "test files" input.
//
// Playwright writes one `<testsuite>` per test file, with the file's path
// (relative to `e2e/`) as its `name` and `failures`/`errors` counts.
//
// The reports come from a PR's CI run, so they are untrusted: only names that
// look like e2e test files are printed, and anything else is dropped.
//
// Usage:
//   node .github/scripts/vrt-failed-files.mjs <reports-dir>

import { readdirSync, readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { join } from 'node:path';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';

const TESTSUITE_TAG = /<testsuite\b([^>]*)>/g;
const ATTRIBUTE = /([\w:-]+)\s*=\s*"([^"]*)"/g;
// e.g. budget.test.ts, budget.mobile.test.ts, reports/net-worth.test.ts
const TEST_FILE = /^[\w.-]+(?:\/[\w.-]+)*\.test\.tsx?$/;

function parseAttributes(text) {
  const attributes = {};
  for (const [, key, value] of text.matchAll(ATTRIBUTE)) {
    attributes[key] = value;
  }
  return attributes;
}

function isSafeTestFile(name) {
  return TEST_FILE.test(name) && !name.split('/').includes('..');
}

// Returns the sorted, de-duplicated `e2e/<file>` paths of every test suite in
// the given JUnit XML documents that has at least one failure or error
export function failedVrtFiles(xmlDocuments) {
  const files = new Set();
  for (const xml of xmlDocuments) {
    for (const [, attributeText] of xml.matchAll(TESTSUITE_TAG)) {
      const { name, failures, errors } = parseAttributes(attributeText);
      const hasFailed = Number(failures) > 0 || Number(errors) > 0;
      if (hasFailed && name && isSafeTestFile(name)) {
        files.add(`e2e/${name}`);
      }
    }
  }
  return [...files].sort();
}

function readXmlFiles(dir) {
  const documents = [];
  for (const entry of readdirSync(dir, { withFileTypes: true })) {
    const path = join(dir, entry.name);
    if (entry.isDirectory()) {
      documents.push(...readXmlFiles(path));
    } else if (entry.isFile() && entry.name.endsWith('.xml')) {
      documents.push(readFileSync(path, 'utf8'));
    }
  }
  return documents;
}

if (process.argv[1] === fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)) {
  const dir = process.argv[2];
  if (!dir) {
    console.error('Usage: node vrt-failed-files.mjs <reports-dir>');
    process.exit(2);
  }
  console.log(failedVrtFiles(readXmlFiles(dir)).join(' '));
}

// Tests for vrt-failed-files.mjs (issue #153).
// Run with: node --test .github/scripts/
//
// fixtures/vrt-junit.xml is a real report from Playwright 1.61.1's JUnit
// reporter (the version CI uses): `passing.test.ts` has a passing and a
// skipped test, and `reports/failing.mobile.test.ts` has a test that failed
// on both tries (retries: 1, as in playwright.config.ts).

import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import { execFileSync } from 'node:child_process';
import { mkdtempSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync, mkdirSync } from 'node:fs';
import { tmpdir } from 'node:os';
import { join } from 'node:path';
import { describe, it } from 'node:test';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';

import { failedVrtFiles } from './vrt-failed-files.mjs';

const fixture = readFileSync(
  new URL('./fixtures/vrt-junit.xml', import.meta.url),
  'utf8',
);
const script = fileURLToPath(new URL('./vrt-failed-files.mjs', import.meta.url));

function suite(name, { failures = 0, errors = 0 } = {}) {
  return `<testsuite name="${name}" tests="1" failures="${failures}" errors="${errors}"></testsuite>`;
}

describe('failedVrtFiles', () => {
  it('lists only the file with a failed test in a real Playwright report', () => {
    assert.deepEqual(failedVrtFiles([fixture]), [
      'e2e/reports/failing.mobile.test.ts',
    ]);
  });

  it('ignores the <testsuites> wrapper, which also counts failures', () => {
    const xml = `<testsuites failures="1">${suite('a.test.ts')}</testsuites>`;
    assert.deepEqual(failedVrtFiles([xml]), []);
  });

  it('lists files with errors as well as failures', () => {
    const xml = suite('errored.test.ts', { errors: 1 });
    assert.deepEqual(failedVrtFiles([xml]), ['e2e/errored.test.ts']);
  });

  it('merges the reports from all shards, sorted and without duplicates', () => {
    const shard1 = suite('settings.test.ts', { failures: 1 });
    const shard2 =
      suite('budget.test.ts', { failures: 2 }) + suite('ok.test.ts');
    const shard3 = suite('settings.test.ts', { failures: 1 });
    assert.deepEqual(failedVrtFiles([shard1, shard2, shard3]), [
      'e2e/budget.test.ts',
      'e2e/settings.test.ts',
    ]);
  });

  it('returns an empty list when nothing failed', () => {
    assert.deepEqual(failedVrtFiles([suite('a.test.ts'), '']), []);
  });

  it('drops names that are not e2e test files', () => {
    const xml = [
      suite('../../etc/passwd.test.ts', { failures: 1 }),
      suite('a/../b.test.ts', { failures: 1 }),
      suite('evil`$(whoami)`.test.ts', { failures: 1 }),
      suite('with space.test.ts', { failures: 1 }),
      suite('/absolute.test.ts', { failures: 1 }),
      suite('notes.md', { failures: 1 }),
      suite('[link](https://example.com).test.ts', { failures: 1 }),
    ].join('');
    assert.deepEqual(failedVrtFiles([xml]), []);
  });
});

describe('vrt-failed-files.mjs CLI', () => {
  it('reads every .xml file under the folder and prints one line', () => {
    const dir = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'vrt-junit-'));
    mkdirSync(join(dir, 'vrt-junit-1'));
    mkdirSync(join(dir, 'vrt-junit-2'));
    writeFileSync(join(dir, 'vrt-junit-1', 'junit.xml'), fixture);
    writeFileSync(
      join(dir, 'vrt-junit-2', 'junit.xml'),
      suite('budget.test.ts', { failures: 1 }),
    );
    writeFileSync(
      join(dir, 'vrt-junit-2', 'notes.txt'),
      suite('ignored.test.ts', { failures: 1 }),
    );

    const output = execFileSync('node', [script, dir], { encoding: 'utf8' });
    assert.equal(
      output,
      'e2e/budget.test.ts e2e/reports/failing.mobile.test.ts\n',
    );
  });
});

```yaml
# Fork-only workflow (CSCI-435-SE/actual-budget, issue #153).
#
# Regenerates a PR's browser VRT screenshots in the same container, and with
# the same build, as the `vrt` job in e2e-test.yml. It commits the changed
# PNGs to the PR's branch, then starts E2E Tests on that commit (a push made
# with GITHUB_TOKEN doesn't start workflows by itself, but a dispatch does).
# Upstream's `/update-vrt` comment bot (vrt-update-*.yml) can't run here; see
# "Updating VRT screenshots" in STUDENTS.md.
#
# Security: build-web and generate build and run the PR's code, so they only
# get a read-only token. The commit job is the only one that can write, and
# it never runs code from the PR: it re-checks the PNGs, copies them and
# pushes.
name: Update VRT screenshots

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      pr_number:
        description: 'PR number'
        required: true
        type: number
      test_files:
        description: 'Test files to update, separated by spaces (e.g. e2e/budget.test.ts). Leave blank to update all.'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''

permissions: {}

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ inputs.pr_number }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Every file the run may change: a PNG in an e2e `*-snapshots` folder
  SNAPSHOT_PATH: '^packages/desktop-client/e2e/[A-Za-z0-9._-]+-snapshots/[A-Za-z0-9._-]+\.png$'

jobs:
  get-pr:
    name: Check the PR
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      pull-requests: read
    outputs:
      head_sha: ${{ steps.pr.outputs.head_sha }}
      head_ref: ${{ steps.pr.outputs.head_ref }}
      test_files: ${{ steps.pr.outputs.test_files }}
      shards: ${{ steps.pr.outputs.shards }}
    steps:
      - name: Look up the PR and check the inputs
        id: pr
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          PR_NUMBER: ${{ inputs.pr_number }}
          TEST_FILES: ${{ inputs.test_files }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          if ! pr=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/pulls/$PR_NUMBER"); then
            echo "::error::Couldn't find PR #$PR_NUMBER in $GITHUB_REPOSITORY. Check the PR number."
            exit 1
          fi

          state=$(jq -r '.state' <<< "$pr")
          head_repo=$(jq -r '.head.repo.full_name // "a deleted repository"' <<< "$pr")
          head_ref=$(jq -r '.head.ref' <<< "$pr")
          head_sha=$(jq -r '.head.sha' <<< "$pr")

          if [ "$state" != "open" ]; then
            echo "::error::PR #$PR_NUMBER is $state. Only open PRs can be updated; nothing was pushed."
            exit 1
          fi
          if [ "$head_repo" != "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" ]; then
            echo "::error::PR #$PR_NUMBER's branch is in $head_repo, not $GITHUB_REPOSITORY. This workflow can only push to branches in this repository; nothing was pushed."
            exit 1
          fi

          # Accept `budget.test.ts`, `e2e/budget.test.ts` or
          # `packages/desktop-client/e2e/budget.test.ts`, and pass them to
          # Playwright as `e2e/<file>`.
          files=()
          for file in $TEST_FILES; do
            file="${file#packages/desktop-client/}"
            file="${file#e2e/}"
            if ! [[ "$file" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+(/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+)*\.test\.tsx?$ ]] || [[ "/$file/" == */../* ]]; then
              echo "::error::'$file' isn't an e2e test file. Use paths like e2e/budget.test.ts, separated by spaces."
              exit 1
            fi
            files+=("e2e/$file")
          done

          if [ ${#files[@]} -eq 0 ]; then
            # All VRT tests, split into 3 shards like the CI VRT job
            echo "shards=[1, 2, 3]" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "test_files=" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            which_tests="all VRT tests"
          else
            # A few files run in one job, so no shard ends up with no tests
            echo "shards=[1]" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "test_files=${files[*]}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            which_tests="\`${files[*]}\`"
          fi
          {
            echo "head_sha=$head_sha"
            echo "head_ref=$head_ref"
          } >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

          echo "### Updating VRT screenshots for #$PR_NUMBER" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          echo "Branch \`$head_ref\` at \`$head_sha\`, $which_tests." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

  build-web:
    name: Build web bundle
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: get-pr
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@de0fac2e4500dabe0009e67214ff5f5447ce83dd # v6.0.2
        with:
          ref: ${{ needs.get-pr.outputs.head_sha }}
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Check the test files exist
        if: needs.get-pr.outputs.test_files != ''
        env:
          TEST_FILES: ${{ needs.get-pr.outputs.test_files }}
        run: |
          for file in $TEST_FILES; do
            if [ ! -f "packages/desktop-client/$file" ]; then
              echo "::error::packages/desktop-client/$file doesn't exist on the PR's branch."
              exit 1
            fi
          done
      - name: Set up environment
        uses: ./.github/actions/setup
        with:
          download-translations: 'false'
      - name: Build browser bundle
        # Same as the build-web job in e2e-test.yml; see the notes there.
        env:
          REACT_APP_NETLIFY: 'true'
        run: yarn build:browser --skip-translations
      - name: Upload build artifact
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: desktop-client-build
          path: packages/desktop-client/build/
          retention-days: 1
          overwrite: true

  generate:
    name: Generate screenshots (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/${{ strategy.job-total }})
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [get-pr, build-web]
    permissions:
      contents: read
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: ${{ fromJson(needs.get-pr.outputs.shards) }}
    # Same container as the vrt job in e2e-test.yml; screenshots made
    # anywhere else don't match CI's.
    container:
      image: mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.61.1-jammy
    env:
      E2E_USE_BUILD: '1'
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@de0fac2e4500dabe0009e67214ff5f5447ce83dd # v6.0.2
        with:
          ref: ${{ needs.get-pr.outputs.head_sha }}
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Set up environment
        uses: ./.github/actions/setup
        with:
          download-translations: 'false'
      - name: Trust the repository directory
        run: git config --global --add safe.directory "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
      - name: Download web build
        uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: desktop-client-build
          path: packages/desktop-client/build/
      - name: Set E2E port
        env:
          SHARD: ${{ matrix.shard }}
        run: echo "E2E_PORT=$((3000 + SHARD))" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
      - name: Regenerate changed screenshots
        id: vrt
        env:
          SHARD: ${{ matrix.shard }}
          SHARD_TOTAL: ${{ strategy.job-total }}
          TEST_FILES: ${{ needs.get-pr.outputs.test_files }}
        # With --update-snapshots=changed, a screenshot that differs is
        # rewritten and its check passes, so a failing test here broke for
        # another reason. Keep going so the other screenshots are still
        # updated, and report the failure in the summary.
        run: |
          set +e
          # shellcheck disable=SC2086 # TEST_FILES is a checked, space-separated list
          yarn vrt --update-snapshots=changed --shard="$SHARD/$SHARD_TOTAL" $TEST_FILES
          echo "exit_code=$?" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - name: Check that only screenshots changed
        id: changes
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          deleted=$(git ls-files --deleted)
          changed=$(git ls-files --modified --others --exclude-standard | sort -u)
          not_screenshots=$(grep -vE "$SNAPSHOT_PATH" <<< "$changed" || true)

          if [ -n "$deleted" ] || [ -n "$not_screenshots" ]; then
            echo "::error::The VRT run changed files that aren't PNG screenshots in an e2e *-snapshots folder, so nothing was pushed."
            printf 'Deleted:\n%s\nNot screenshots:\n%s\n' "$deleted" "$not_screenshots"
            exit 1
          fi

          if [ -z "$changed" ]; then
            echo "has_changes=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "No screenshots changed in this shard."
            exit 0
          fi

          echo "has_changes=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          mkdir -p "$RUNNER_TEMP/vrt-shard"
          while IFS= read -r file; do
            cp --parents "$file" "$RUNNER_TEMP/vrt-shard/"
          done <<< "$changed"
          echo "Changed screenshots:"
          echo "$changed"
      - name: Upload changed screenshots
        if: steps.changes.outputs.has_changes == 'true'
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: vrt-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/vrt-shard/
          retention-days: 1
          overwrite: true
      - name: Report failing tests
        if: steps.vrt.outputs.exit_code != '0'
        env:
          SHARD: ${{ matrix.shard }}
        run: |
          echo "::warning::Some VRT tests in shard $SHARD failed for a reason other than a screenshot difference. Their screenshots weren't updated. See the 'vrt-test-results-$SHARD' artifact."
          echo "⚠️ Shard $SHARD: some tests failed for a reason other than a screenshot difference, so their screenshots weren't updated. See the \`vrt-test-results-$SHARD\` artifact." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
      - name: Upload test results
        if: steps.vrt.outputs.exit_code != '0'
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: vrt-test-results-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: packages/desktop-client/test-results/
          retention-days: 7
          overwrite: true

  commit:
    name: Commit screenshots
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [get-pr, generate]
    permissions:
      contents: write # push the screenshots to the PR's branch
      actions: write # start E2E Tests on the new commit
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@de0fac2e4500dabe0009e67214ff5f5447ce83dd # v6.0.2
        with:
          ref: ${{ needs.get-pr.outputs.head_sha }}
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Find the changed screenshots
        id: artifacts
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          count=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/actions/runs/$GITHUB_RUN_ID/artifacts" \
            --jq '[.artifacts[] | select(.name | startswith("vrt-shard-"))] | length')
          echo "count=$count" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - name: Download the changed screenshots
        if: steps.artifacts.outputs.count != '0'
        uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          pattern: vrt-shard-*
          merge-multiple: true
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/vrt-shards
      - name: Commit and push
        id: push
        if: steps.artifacts.outputs.count != '0'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          HEAD_REF: ${{ needs.get-pr.outputs.head_ref }}
          PR_NUMBER: ${{ inputs.pr_number }}
          RUN_URL: ${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          shards="$RUNNER_TEMP/vrt-shards"

          # These files came from jobs that ran the PR's code, so check them
          # again before anything is written: only regular PNG files at
          # screenshot paths.
          not_screenshots=$(cd "$shards" && find . -mindepth 1 ! -type d | sed 's|^\./||' | grep -vE "$SNAPSHOT_PATH" || true)
          not_files=$(cd "$shards" && find . -mindepth 1 ! -type d ! -type f)
          if [ -n "$not_screenshots" ] || [ -n "$not_files" ]; then
            echo "::error::The screenshot artifacts contain files that aren't PNG screenshots, so nothing was pushed."
            printf '%s\n' "$not_screenshots" "$not_files"
            exit 1
          fi

          cp -r "$shards/." .
          git add -- 'packages/desktop-client/e2e/*-snapshots/*.png'

          if git diff --staged --quiet; then
            echo "pushed=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            exit 0
          fi

          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
          git config user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
          git commit --quiet -m "Update VRT screenshots" -m "Generated by $RUN_URL for #$PR_NUMBER."

          # Final guard: the commit only changes screenshots
          not_screenshots=$(git diff --name-only HEAD~1 HEAD | grep -vE "$SNAPSHOT_PATH" || true)
          if [ -n "$not_screenshots" ]; then
            echo "::error::The commit would change files that aren't screenshots, so nothing was pushed: $not_screenshots"
            exit 1
          fi

          # A plain push (no force), so it fails if someone pushed to the
          # branch after this run started
          if ! git push --quiet "https://x-access-token:${GH_TOKEN}@github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}.git" "HEAD:refs/heads/${HEAD_REF}"; then
            echo "::error::Couldn't push to $HEAD_REF. If someone pushed to it after this run started, run the workflow again; nothing was pushed."
            exit 1
          fi

          echo "pushed=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          {
            echo "### ✅ Pushed $(git diff --name-only HEAD~1 HEAD | wc -l) updated screenshots to \`$HEAD_REF\`"
            echo "Commit: $GITHUB_SERVER_URL/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/commit/$(git rev-parse HEAD)"
            echo
            git diff --name-only HEAD~1 HEAD | sed 's/^/- `/; s/$/`/'
          } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
      - name: Report no changes
        if: steps.artifacts.outputs.count == '0' || steps.push.outputs.pushed == 'false'
        run: |
          echo "No screenshots differ from the ones on the branch, so nothing was pushed."
          echo "### No screenshots changed, so nothing was pushed." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
      - name: Start E2E Tests on the new commit
        if: steps.push.outputs.pushed == 'true'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          HEAD_REF: ${{ needs.get-pr.outputs.head_ref }}
        run: |

const step = (job, id) => wf.jobs[job].steps.find(s => s.id === id || s.name === id).run;

  console.log(`${cond ? 'PASS' : 'FAIL'}  ${label}${!cond && detail ? `\n      ${detail}` : ''}`);

}

function runStep(script, { cwd, env }) {
  const tmp = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'step-'));
  const file = join(tmp, 'step.sh');
  writeFileSync(file, script);
  const out = join(tmp, 'out'), sum = join(tmp, 'sum');
  writeFileSync(out, ''); writeFileSync(sum, '');
  const r = spawnSync('bash', ['--noprofile', '--norc', '-eo', 'pipefail', file], {
    cwd, encoding: 'utf8',
    env: { ...process.env, GITHUB_OUTPUT: out, GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY: sum, RUNNER_TEMP: tmp,
      GITHUB_REPOSITORY: 'CSCI-435-SE/actual-budget', GITHUB_SERVER_URL: 'https://github.com',
      GITHUB_RUN_ID: '1', SNAPSHOT_PATH, ...env },

    .map(l => [l.slice(0, l.indexOf('=')), l.slice(l.indexOf('=') + 1)]));

# Writing Release Notes for actualbudget/actual

Release notes are the user-facing changelog. Each code change adds one Markdown file to `upcoming-release-notes/`, and these get collected into the published changelog at the next release. The authoritative source is the **Writing Good Release Notes** section of `packages/docs/docs/contributing/index.md`. Read it if anything below is unclear.

## The file

Create `upcoming-release-notes/<slug>.md`, where `<slug>` is a **short, descriptive kebab-case slug** naming the change (e.g. `add-payee-autocomplete.md`, `fix-mobile-category-delete.md`). Do **not** use a PR number, since the PR link is resolved automatically at release time. (Numeric filenames like `1234.md` still work, but a slug is preferred.)

```markdown
---
category: Features
authors: [YourGitHubUsername]
---

Add payee autocomplete to the transaction entry form
```

- **`category`**: exactly one of `Features` (new feature), `Enhancements` (improvement to an existing feature), `Bugfix` (bug fix), or `Maintenance` (internal change with no user-visible effect).
- **`authors`**: array of the GitHub username(s) who did the work.

## Writing the entry

The body is the changelog line. It is read by everyday users, not developers.

- **One sentence.** Short and clear. No paragraphs, no bullet lists, no long prose.
- **Plain language, no technical detail.** Describe what changed for the user, not how it was built. Avoid file names, function names, internal component names, and implementation jargon. (Exception: `Maintenance` entries may be technical, since they are for internal changes.)
- **Phrase it as a command.** Start with a present-tense verb: "Add …", "Fix …", "Show …", not "Added …" or "Adds …".
- Generally match the PR title, but reword it if that reads more clearly to a user.

Good: `Fix incorrect balance when reconciling an account with future transactions`
Too technical: `Fix off-by-one in reconcileTransactions() when txn.date > today`


---

import { failedVrtFiles } from './vrt-failed-files.mjs';

const fixture = readFileSync(
  new URL('./fixtures/vrt-junit.xml', import.meta.url),
  'utf8',
);
const script = fileURLToPath(
  new URL('./vrt-failed-files.mjs', import.meta.url),
);

function suite(name, { failures = 0, errors = 0 } = {}) {
  return `<testsuite name="${name}" tests="1" failures="${failures}" errors="${errors}"></testsuite>`;
}

describe('failedVrtFiles', () => {
  it('lists only the file with a failed test in a real Playwright report', () => {
    expect(failedVrtFiles([fixture])).toEqual([
      'e2e/reports/failing.mobile.test.ts',
    ]);
  });

  it('ignores the <testsuites> wrapper, which also counts failures', () => {
    const xml = `<testsuites failures="1">${suite('a.test.ts')}</testsuites>`;
    expect(failedVrtFiles([xml])).toEqual([]);
  });

  it('lists files with errors as well as failures', () => {
    const xml = suite('errored.test.ts', { errors: 1 });
    expect(failedVrtFiles([xml])).toEqual(['e2e/errored.test.ts']);
  });

  it('merges the reports from all shards, sorted and without duplicates', () => {
    const shard1 = suite('settings.test.ts', { failures: 1 });
    const shard2 =
      suite('budget.test.ts', { failures: 2 }) + suite('ok.test.ts');
    const shard3 = suite('settings.test.ts', { failures: 1 });
    expect(failedVrtFiles([shard1, shard2, shard3])).toEqual([
      'e2e/budget.test.ts',
      'e2e/settings.test.ts',
    ]);
  });

  it('returns an empty list when nothing failed', () => {
    expect(failedVrtFiles([suite('a.test.ts'), ''])).toEqual([]);
  });

  it('drops names that are not e2e test files', () => {
    const xml = [
      suite('../../etc/passwd.test.ts', { failures: 1 }),
      suite('a/../b.test.ts', { failures: 1 }),
      suite('evil`$(whoami)`.test.ts', { failures: 1 }),
      suite('with space.test.ts', { failures: 1 }),
      suite('/absolute.test.ts', { failures: 1 }),
      suite('notes.md', { failures: 1 }),
      suite('[link](https://example.com).test.ts', { failures: 1 }),
    ].join('');
    expect(failedVrtFiles([xml])).toEqual([]);
  });
});

describe('vrt-failed-files.mjs CLI', () => {
  it('reads every .xml file under the folder and prints one line', () => {
    const dir = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'vrt-junit-'));
    mkdirSync(join(dir, 'vrt-junit-1'));
    mkdirSync(join(dir, 'vrt-junit-2'));
    writeFileSync(join(dir, 'vrt-junit-1', 'junit.xml'), fixture);
    writeFileSync(
      join(dir, 'vrt-junit-2', 'junit.xml'),
      suite('budget.test.ts', { failures: 1 }),
    );
    writeFileSync(
      join(dir, 'vrt-junit-2', 'notes.txt'),
      suite('ignored.test.ts', { failures: 1 }),
    );

    const output = execFileSync('node', [script, dir], { encoding: 'utf8' });
    expect(output).toBe(
      'e2e/budget.test.ts e2e/reports/failing.mobile.test.ts\n',
    );
  });
});

# Committing Changes in actualbudget/actual

Before creating any git commit or pull request in this repo, read:

**`.github/agents/pr-and-commit-rules.md`**

It is the authoritative source for the rules you must apply yourself: the `[AI]` PR-title prefix and leaving the PR template blank (and the Chinese exception). The mechanical commit/git rules are enforced by tooling and aren't restated there. Read it on every commit/PR session so any updates are picked up automatically.

## The one rule worth restating

Every commit message and every pull request title MUST begin with `[AI]`. Commit messages are checked by the git-guard hook (a missing prefix is blocked before the commit lands), so the one that needs _your_ attention is the PR title — nothing checks it for you, and the cost of forgetting it is high since the PR has to be renamed by hand. Examples:

- `[AI] Fix type error in account validation` — correct
- `Fix type error in account validation` — wrong, missing prefix

The PR-template rule and the rest live in the rules file. Read it before each commit/PR rather than relying on this skill's summary, because the rules file evolves and this skill deliberately does not restate it.

## Why this matters

Maintainers triage AI-authored contributions separately, and the `[AI]` prefix is what makes that triage fast — it also drives the automatic `"AI generated"` PR label, so getting the prefix right is the one action that gates the whole triage path. Without it the PR looks like a normal human contribution and the wrong review process gets applied. The "do not fill in the PR template" rule exists because the human is the one who actually tested the change and can write the Description / Testing / Checklist sections honestly — an AI-filled template misrepresents who did what.

The rules file is short. Read it.

1. Go to https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/actual-budget and click **Fork** (top right).
2. Set **Owner** to `TigerK9` and keep the name `actual-budget`.
3. Leave **"Copy the `master` branch only"** checked. You'll only need `master` and one test branch.
4. Click **Create fork**.

**Why a fork:** GitHub only lets you start a `workflow_dispatch` workflow (one with a "Run workflow" button) when the file is on the repo's **default branch**. In your fork, you can put this code on `master` without touching the team's `master`.

## Step 2: Turn on Actions in the fork
GitHub disables workflows in new forks so copied code can't run without your say-so.
1. In your fork, open the **Actions** tab.

After you commit, I'll run:

- `HEAD:master` pushes this branch's commit onto the fork's `master`, so "Update VRT screenshots" shows up in the fork's Actions tab. `origin` isn't touched.

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-11-09 23:07:46Z)**_

"Approved checks" means the 8 workflows GitHub is holding on your test PR, the ones in the "8 workflows awaiting approval" message.

**Why they're waiting:** when the update workflow pushed the screenshot commit, GitHub created the usual PR checks for it (Build, Test, E2E Tests, Fork CI guard, and so on). Because that commit was pushed by `github-actions[bot]` and not by you, GitHub won't run them until someone with access says it's OK. That's a safety rule so a bot can't run code on its own.

**What to do:**
1. Open your test PR (TigerK9/actual-budget, PR #1).
2. Scroll to the checks box near the bottom. It should say something like **"8 workflows awaiting approval"**.
3. Click **Approve and run workflows**. It's safe, because the commit is your own code plus 3 PNGs.

**"When they finish":** the 8 checks then start running. E2E Tests takes several minutes. Once they're all green or red, send me:
- whether **Functional (shard 2/3)** passed or failed, and if it failed, whether it's the same `budget.test.ts` test
- whether the other checks passed

**Why it matters:**
- If shard 2 **passes** on the same commit, the test is flaky, which is good evidence for the bug report.
- If it **fails again**, the bug is consistent, which is also useful to report.
- Either way, the commit ends up with its full set of checks, which is what your PR evidence should show.

// Integration tests for .github/workflows/update-vrt.yml (issue #153).
// Run with: yarn vitest run --root .github/scripts
//
// Each test takes a step's real `run:` script out of the workflow and runs it
// with the shell GitHub would use, against a fake PR (a stub `gh`), a
// throwaway git repository and, for pushes, a local bare repository standing
// in for GitHub. Nothing here talks to the network.

import { execFileSync, spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';
import {
  chmodSync,
  mkdirSync,
  mkdtempSync,
  readFileSync,
  rmSync,
  symlinkSync,
  writeFileSync,
} from 'node:fs';
import { tmpdir } from 'node:os';
import { dirname, join } from 'node:path';

import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import { parse } from 'yaml';

const workflow = parse(
  readFileSync(
    new URL('../workflows/update-vrt.yml', import.meta.url),
    'utf8',
  ),
);
const REPO = 'CSCI-435-SE/actual-budget';
const BRANCH = 'feat/issue-1-example';
const SNAPSHOTS = 'packages/desktop-client/e2e/budget.test.ts-snapshots';

// How GitHub runs a `run:` script for each `shell` value. With no shell set,
// container jobs use sh and other jobs use bash without pipefail.
const SHELL_COMMANDS = {
  bash: ['bash', '--noprofile', '--norc', '-eo', 'pipefail'],
  sh: ['sh', '-e'],
  unset: ['bash', '-e'],
};

function getStep(jobId, stepId) {
  const job = workflow.jobs[jobId];
  const step = job.steps.find(s => s.id === stepId);
  const shell =
    step.shell ??
    job.defaults?.run?.shell ??
    workflow.defaults?.run?.shell ??
    (job.container ? 'sh' : 'unset');
  return { script: step.run, shell };
}

function runStep({ script, shell }, { cwd, env = {} }) {
  const temp = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'update-vrt-step-'));
  const scriptFile = join(temp, 'step.sh');
  const outputFile = join(temp, 'output');
  const summaryFile = join(temp, 'summary');
  writeFileSync(scriptFile, script);
  writeFileSync(outputFile, '');
  writeFileSync(summaryFile, '');

  const [command, ...args] = SHELL_COMMANDS[shell];
  const result = spawnSync(command, [...args, scriptFile], {
    cwd,
    encoding: 'utf8',
    env: {
      ...process.env,
      GITHUB_OUTPUT: outputFile,
      GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY: summaryFile,
      GITHUB_REPOSITORY: REPO,
      GITHUB_SERVER_URL: 'https://github.com',
      GITHUB_RUN_ID: '1',
      RUNNER_TEMP: temp,
      SNAPSHOT_PATH: workflow.env.SNAPSHOT_PATH,
      ...env,
    },
  });

  const outputs = {};
  for (const line of readFileSync(outputFile, 'utf8').split('\n')) {
    const index = line.indexOf('=');
    if (index > 0) {
      outputs[line.slice(0, index)] = line.slice(index + 1);
    }
  }
  return {
    exitCode: result.status,
    log: result.stdout + result.stderr,
    outputs,
    summary: readFileSync(summaryFile, 'utf8'),
    runnerTemp: temp,
  };
}

function git(cwd, ...args) {
  return execFileSync('git', args, { cwd, encoding: 'utf8' }).trim();
}

// A repository with two committed screenshots and a test file
function makeRepo() {
  const dir = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'update-vrt-repo-'));
  git(dir, 'init', '-q', '-b', 'main');
  git(dir, 'config', 'user.name', 'Test');
  git(dir, 'config', 'user.email', 'test@example.com');
  mkdirSync(join(dir, SNAPSHOTS), { recursive: true });
  writeFileSync(join(dir, SNAPSHOTS, 'a-chromium-linux.png'), 'old a');
  writeFileSync(join(dir, SNAPSHOTS, 'b-chromium-linux.png'), 'old b');
  writeFileSync(join(dir, 'packages/desktop-client/e2e/budget.test.ts'), '');
  writeFileSync(join(dir, '.gitignore'), 'test-results/\n');
  git(dir, 'add', '.');
  git(dir, 'commit', '-qm', 'Initial commit');
  return dir;
}

function listFiles(dir) {
  return execFileSync('find', [dir, '-type', 'f', '-printf', '%P\n'], {
    encoding: 'utf8',
  })
    .trim()
    .split('\n')
    .filter(Boolean)
    .sort((a, b) => a.localeCompare(b));
}

describe('update-vrt.yml: Check the PR', () => {
  const step = getStep('get-pr', 'pr');
  const fakeBin = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'update-vrt-bin-'));
  writeFileSync(
    join(fakeBin, 'gh'),
    '#!/bin/sh\nif [ "$[REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]_PR" = "missing" ]; then echo "HTTP 404" >&2; exit 1; fi\nprintf "%s" "$[REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]_PR"\n',
  );
  chmodSync(join(fakeBin, 'gh'), 0o755);

  function checkPr({ state = 'open', repo = REPO, testFiles = '' } = {}) {
    const pr =
      state === 'missing'
        ? 'missing'
        : JSON.stringify({
            state,
            head: {
              ref: BRANCH,
              sha: 'abc123',
              repo: repo === null ? null : { full_name: repo },
            },
          });
    return runStep(step, {
      cwd: tmpdir(),
      env: {
        PATH: `${fakeBin}:${process.env.PATH}`,
        [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]_PR: pr,
        PR_NUMBER: '42',
        TEST_FILES: testFiles,
      },
    });
  }

  it('accepts an open PR from this repository and runs all VRT tests in 3 shards', () => {
    const result = checkPr();
    expect(result.exitCode).toBe(0);
    expect(result.outputs).toEqual({
      shards: '[1, 2, 3]',
      test_files: '',
      head_sha: 'abc123',
      head_ref: BRANCH,
    });
    expect(result.summary).toContain('#42');
  });

  it('runs only the given test files, in one shard, as e2e/<file> paths', () => {
    const result = checkPr({
      testFiles:
        'budget.test.ts  e2e/settings.mobile.test.ts packages/desktop-client/e2e/reports/net-worth.test.ts',
    });
    expect(result.exitCode).toBe(0);
    expect(result.outputs.shards).toBe('[1]');
    expect(result.outputs.test_files).toBe(
      'e2e/budget.test.ts e2e/settings.mobile.test.ts e2e/reports/net-worth.test.ts',
    );
  });

  it.each([
    [{ state: 'closed' }, 'PR #42 is closed'],
    [{ repo: 'someone/actual-budget' }, 'is in someone/actual-budget'],
    [{ repo: null }, 'is in a deleted repository'],
    [{ state: 'missing' }, "Couldn't find PR #42"],
  ])('refuses %o with a clear error', (pr, message) => {
    const result = checkPr(pr);
    expect(result.exitCode).not.toBe(0);
    expect(result.log).toContain(message);
    expect(result.outputs.head_ref).toBeUndefined();
  });

  it.each([
    'e2e/../../etc/passwd.test.ts',
    'budget.ts',
    '$(touch /tmp/pwned).test.ts',
    'e2e/budget.test.ts;rm',
    '--update-snapshots=all',
  ])('refuses the test file %s', testFile => {
    const result = checkPr({ testFiles: testFile });
    expect(result.exitCode).not.toBe(0);
    expect(result.log).toContain("isn't an e2e test file");
  });
});

describe('update-vrt.yml: Check that only screenshots changed', () => {
  const step = getStep('generate', 'changes');

  it('runs with bash, not the container default sh', () => {
    // Regression: under sh the step stopped at `set -o pipefail`

describe('update-vrt.yml: Commit and push', () => {
  const step = getStep('commit', 'push');

  // A checkout of the PR branch, a bare "GitHub" repository the push goes to
  // (via git's url.insteadOf), and the downloaded shard artifacts
  function setUp(artifactFiles) {
    const origin = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'update-vrt-origin-'));
    git(origin, 'init', '-q', '--bare');
    const repo = makeRepo();
    git(repo, 'push', '-q', origin, `HEAD:refs/heads/${BRANCH}`);

    const gitConfig = join(mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'update-vrt-gc-')), 'c');
    writeFileSync(
      gitConfig,
      `[url "${origin}"]\n\tinsteadOf = https://x-access-token:[REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]@github.com/${REPO}.git\n`,
    );

    const result = runStep(
      {
        ...step,
        // Write the artifacts where the step looks for them
        script: `mkdir -p "$RUNNER_TEMP/vrt-shards" && cp -a "$ARTIFACTS/." "$RUNNER_TEMP/vrt-shards/"\n${step.script}`,
      },
      {
        cwd: repo,
        env: {
          ARTIFACTS: makeArtifacts(artifactFiles),
          GH_TOKEN: '[REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]',
          HEAD_REF: BRANCH,
          PR_NUMBER: '42',
          RUN_URL: 'https://github.com/run/1',
          GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL: gitConfig,
        },
      },
    );
    const branchLog = git(origin, 'log', '--format=%s', BRANCH).split('\n');
    const lastCommitFiles = git(
      origin,
      'show',
      '--name-only',
      '--format=',
      BRANCH,
    )
      .split('\n')
      .sort((a, b) => a.localeCompare(b));
    return { result, branchLog, lastCommitFiles, origin };
  }

  function makeArtifacts(files) {
    const dir = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'update-vrt-artifacts-'));
    for (const [path, content] of Object.entries(files)) {
      mkdirSync(dirname(join(dir, path)), { recursive: true });
      if (content === null) {
        symlinkSync('/etc/passwd', join(dir, path));
      } else {
        writeFileSync(join(dir, path), content);
      }
    }
    return dir;
  }

  it('pushes one commit that changes only the screenshots', () => {
    const newSnapshot =
      'packages/desktop-client/e2e/new.test.ts-snapshots/n-chromium-linux.png';
    const { result, branchLog, lastCommitFiles } = setUp({
      [`${SNAPSHOTS}/a-chromium-linux.png`]: 'new a',
      [newSnapshot]: 'new n',
    });

    expect(result.exitCode).toBe(0);
    expect(result.outputs.pushed).toBe('true');
    expect(branchLog).toEqual(['Update VRT screenshots', 'Initial commit']);
    expect(lastCommitFiles).toEqual([
      `${SNAPSHOTS}/a-chromium-linux.png`,
      newSnapshot,
    ]);
    expect(result.summary).toContain('Pushed 2 updated screenshots');
  });

  it("pushes nothing when the screenshots match the branch's", () => {
    const { result, branchLog } = setUp({
      [`${SNAPSHOTS}/a-chromium-linux.png`]: 'old a',
    });
    expect(result.exitCode).toBe(0);
    expect(result.outputs.pushed).toBe('false');
    expect(branchLog).toEqual(['Initial commit']);
  });

  it.each([
    ['a non-PNG file', { 'package.json': '{}' }],
    ['a workflow file', { '.github/workflows/evil.yml': '' }],
    ['a symlink named like a screenshot', { [`${SNAPSHOTS}/c.png`]: null }],
  ])('refuses artifacts containing %s and pushes nothing', (_, extraFiles) => {
    const { result, branchLog } = setUp({
      [`${SNAPSHOTS}/a-chromium-linux.png`]: 'new a',
      ...extraFiles,
    });
    expect(result.exitCode).not.toBe(0);
    expect(result.log).toContain("aren't PNG screenshots");
    expect(branchLog).toEqual(['Initial commit']);
  });
});

## 2. PR

**Title:** `[AI] feat: add Update VRT screenshots workflow (#153)`
**Milestone:** Sprint 3 *(doesn't exist yet — needs to be created; only "Sprint 2" is open)*
**Reviewer:** **[Liam]** pick a teammate you haven't had review you yet this semester

### Description

Upstream's `/update-vrt` comment bot can't run in our fork (its jobs are limited to
`actualbudget/actual` and need Depot runners), and screenshots made in our arm64 dev containers
don't match CI. The only working way to update VRT screenshots was copying a temporary workflow
into the PR (#116). This PR adds a permanent **Update VRT screenshots** workflow that anyone can
start from the Actions tab with a PR number.

- **`.github/workflows/update-vrt.yml` (new).** Checks the PR is open and from this repo, builds it
  and runs VRT with `--update-snapshots=changed` in CI's container (`playwright:v1.61.1-jammy`,
  same build steps as `e2e-test.yml`), then pushes one commit with only the changed PNGs and starts
  E2E Tests on it. Optional "Test files" input runs only those files in one shard. The jobs that run
  the PR's code only get a read-only token; the job that pushes never runs PR code and re-checks
  that every file is a PNG in a `*-snapshots` folder.
- **`e2e-test.yml`:** `workflow_dispatch` trigger, so the workflow can start the checks on its commit.
- **`e2e-vrt-comment.yml`:** replaces "comment `/update-vrt`" with step-by-step instructions and
  the failed test files, read from the VRT JUnit reports by `.github/scripts/vrt-failed-files.mjs`.
- **`fork-ci-guard.yml`:** also runs the tests in `.github/scripts` (lage only runs workspace tests).
- **`STUDENTS.md`:** new "Updating VRT screenshots" section.
- `yaml` devDependency (tests read the workflow file); release note.

AI disclosure: written with Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5); see the AI Assistance comment for the log.
**[Liam]** add what you reviewed/changed yourself.

### Related issue(s)

Closes #153

### Tech Debt

**Introduced:**
- Two upstream workflow files are edited (`e2e-test.yml` trigger, `e2e-vrt-comment.yml` message and
  steps). They can conflict at upstream syncs; the edits are marked "Fork-only (issue #153)".
- After a bot commit, E2E runs twice: once started by the workflow, once when someone approves the
  held PR checks.
- Screenshots are made from the PR branch as it is, while PR checks test the branch merged with
  `master`. If `master` changed screenshots in the meantime they can differ; `STUDENTS.md` says to
  merge `master` first.
- An E2E run started by the workflow doesn't get a VRT Comment if it fails (the comment only runs
  for `pull_request` runs). The red check is still visible on the PR.
- The `.github/scripts` tests add a job (~1–2 min) to the Fork CI guard workflow.

**Encountered:**
- Upstream's `/update-vrt` workflows can't run here; replaced rather than adapted (issue Design).
- `budget.test.ts:466` ("switches to the mobile layout below the small breakpoint") failed in
  Functional shard 2 on the bot's commit in both E2E runs, but passed one commit earlier. The bot's
  commit only changed 3 PNGs, which Functional tests don't read (`toMatchThemeScreenshots` is a
  no-op without `VRT`). Not changed here; reported as #___ **[Liam: file the bug and fill in]**.
- Pre-existing shellcheck notes in `e2e-test.yml` / the comment's "Extract metadata" step left as is.

// Integration tests for the "Write the comment" step of
// .github/workflows/e2e-vrt-comment.yml (issue #153).
// Run with: yarn vitest run --root .github/scripts
//
// Runs the step's real script the way GitHub does (bash -e, from the repo
// root) and checks the comment it writes. The step reads the JUnit reports
// from /tmp/vrt-junit and writes /tmp/vrt-comment.md, so these tests use
// those paths and clean them up.

import { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';
import {
  copyFileSync,
  mkdirSync,
  mkdtempSync,
  readFileSync,
  rmSync,
  writeFileSync,
} from 'node:fs';
import { tmpdir } from 'node:os';
import { join } from 'node:path';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';

import { afterEach, describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import { parse } from 'yaml';

const repoRoot = fileURLToPath(new URL('../..', import.meta.url));
const workflow = parse(
  readFileSync(
    new URL('../workflows/e2e-vrt-comment.yml', import.meta.url),
    'utf8',
  ),
);
const script = workflow.jobs.comment.steps.find(
  step => step.name === 'Write the comment',
).run;
const fixture = fileURLToPath(
  new URL('./fixtures/vrt-junit.xml', import.meta.url),
);
const REPORTS_DIR = '/tmp/vrt-junit';
const COMMENT_FILE = '/tmp/vrt-comment.md';
const WORKFLOW_URL =
  'https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/actual-budget/actions/workflows/update-vrt.yml';

function writeComment() {
  const scriptFile = join(mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'vrt-comment-')), 's.sh');
  writeFileSync(scriptFile, script);
  const result = spawnSync('bash', ['-e', scriptFile], {
    cwd: repoRoot,
    encoding: 'utf8',
    env: {
      ...process.env,
      ARTIFACT_URL: 'https://github.com/example/artifacts/1',
      DEFAULT_BRANCH: 'master',
      PR_NUMBER: '160',
      WORKFLOW_URL,
    },
  });
  expect(result.status, result.stderr).toBe(0);
  return readFileSync(COMMENT_FILE, 'utf8');
}

afterEach(() => {
  rmSync(REPORTS_DIR, { recursive: true, force: true });
  rmSync(COMMENT_FILE, { force: true });
});

describe('e2e-vrt-comment.yml: Write the comment', () => {
  it('points to the Update VRT screenshots workflow instead of /update-vrt', () => {
    const comment = writeComment();
    expect(comment).toContain(
      `[Actions → Update VRT screenshots](${WORKFLOW_URL})`,
    );
    expect(comment).not.toContain('/update-vrt');
  });

  it('keeps the sticky-comment marker and the report link', () => {
    const comment = writeComment();
    expect(comment.startsWith('<!-- vrt-comment -->\n')).toBe(true);
    expect(comment).toContain(
      '[View the test report](https://github.com/example/artifacts/1)',
    );
  });

  it('fills in the PR number and the default branch', () => {
    const comment = writeComment();
    expect(comment).toContain(
      'Leave **Use workflow from** on `master` and enter `160` as the **PR number**',
    );
  });

  it('lists the failed test files, ready to paste, when reports exist', () => {
    mkdirSync(join(REPORTS_DIR, 'vrt-junit-2'), { recursive: true });
    copyFileSync(fixture, join(REPORTS_DIR, 'vrt-junit-2', 'junit.xml'));

    const comment = writeComment();
    expect(comment).toContain(
      '3. For **Test files**, paste the files that failed, so only they are run:\n' +
        '   ```\n' +
        '   e2e/reports/failing.mobile.test.ts\n' +
        '   ```\n',
    );
  });

  it('says to leave Test files blank when there are no reports', () => {
    const comment = writeComment();
    expect(comment).toContain(
      '3. Leave **Test files** blank to update every screenshot.',
    );
    expect(comment).not.toContain('paste the files that failed');
  });

  it('tells people to approve held checks and to pull the bot commit', () => {
    const comment = writeComment();
    expect(comment).toContain('click **Approve and run workflows**');
    expect(comment).toContain('Run `git pull` before you push again');
  });
});

````

Yes, this failure is fine. It comes from how we set up the fork, not from the workflow you're adding.

**Why it failed:**
- Compare Sizes measures bundle size on the PR and on its **base** commit. For the base it needs an existing successful `Build` run, and the annotation says it couldn't find one: *"No successful build.yml run found for feat/issue-153-update-vrt-workflow base 81fa53728…"*.
- `Build` runs only on pushes to `master` and on pull requests (`build.yml`). On your fork, the test PR's base was our feature branch, standing in for `master`. That branch is neither `master` nor the head of a PR, so `Build` never ran on `81fa53728`. Compare Sizes waited 30 minutes, then gave up.
- The earlier Compare Sizes run on the test PR (commit `3a7f4eb33`) failed the same way, so this has nothing to do with the screenshot commits.

**Why the team PR won't have this problem:** there the base is `master`, which gets a `Build` run on every merge. Compare Sizes has passed on the team's recent PRs (for example, `feat/issue-125-modified-label` on Nov 9). It also isn't part of #153's acceptance criteria, and no check in the team repo is required for merging.

If you want, I can add it to the fork section of the PR draft, under the differences from the team repo:

> Compare Sizes fails on the fork's test PR because its base (the PR branch) never had a `Build` run, which only runs on `master` pushes and PRs. Not an issue in this repo, where the base is `master`.

<ide_selection>The user selected the lines 39 to 209 from /workspaces/actual-budget/pr-153-drafts.md:
### Description

Upstream's `/update-vrt` comment bot can't run in our fork (its jobs are limited to
`actualbudget/actual` and need Depot runners), and screenshots made in our arm64 dev containers
don't match CI. The only working way to update VRT screenshots was copying a temporary workflow
into the PR (#116). This PR adds a permanent **Update VRT screenshots** workflow that anyone can
start from the Actions tab with a PR number.

- **`.github/workflows/update-vrt.yml` (new).** Checks the PR is open and from this repo, builds it
  and runs VRT with `--update-snapshots=changed` in CI's container (`playwright:v1.61.1-jammy`,
  same build steps as `e2e-test.yml`), then pushes one commit with only the changed PNGs and starts
  E2E Tests on it. Optional "Test files" input runs only those files in one shard. The jobs that run
  the PR's code only get a read-only token; the job that pushes never runs PR code and re-checks
  that every file is a PNG in a `*-snapshots` folder.
- **`e2e-test.yml`:** `workflow_dispatch` trigger, so the workflow can start the checks on its commit.
- **`e2e-vrt-comment.yml`:** replaces "comment `/update-vrt`" with step-by-step instructions and
  the failed test files, read from the VRT JUnit reports by `.github/scripts/vrt-failed-files.mjs`.
- **`fork-ci-guard.yml`:** also runs the tests in `.github/scripts` (lage only runs workspace tests).
- **`STUDENTS.md`:** new "Updating VRT screenshots" section.
- `yaml` devDependency (tests read the workflow file); release note.

AI disclosure: written with Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5); see the AI Assistance comment for the log.
**[Liam]** add what you reviewed/changed yourself.

### Design decisions

The issue's Design section (icsasso) chose a new `workflow_dispatch` workflow over adapting
upstream's `/update-vrt`. These are the decisions I made while implementing it.

**1. How the checks run on the bot's screenshot commit**

- **Decision:** after pushing, the workflow starts E2E Tests on the PR branch itself with
  `workflow_dispatch`, which needed a `workflow_dispatch:` trigger in `e2e-test.yml`.
- **Alternatives considered:**
  1. _Re-run the old VRT check by hand_ (the issue's original AC 3). Doesn't work: a re-run tests
     the same commit as the original run, so it tests the old screenshots.
  2. _Push an empty commit or close and reopen the PR by hand._ Works and changes no upstream file,
     but every person has to remember an extra step after each update.
  3. _A personal access token secret_ so the bot's push starts CI. Needs a repo admin to create
     and rotate a token tied to one person's account.
- **Rationale:** `workflow_dispatch` is the one event GitHub lets `GITHUB_TOKEN` start, so it needs
  no secret and no manual step. The cost is three lines in one upstream file.
- **Consequences:** _Easier:_ the checks start on their own after an update. _Harder:_ one more
  upstream edit that can conflict at syncs; branches made before this merges can't be started this
  way (the workflow warns and says to merge `master`); and GitHub still holds the other PR checks
  for approval, so E2E can run twice.

**2. Which job gets write access**

- **Decision:** split the workflow so the jobs that build and run the PR's code (`build-web`,
  `generate`) have a read-only token, and only the `commit` job can push. It never runs PR code: it
  re-checks the downloaded files are PNG screenshots, then commits and pushes.
- **Alternatives considered:**
  1. _One job that runs the tests and pushes_ (like #116's temporary workflow). Simpler, but the
     PR's code would run with a token that can push to any branch.
  2. _Upstream's two-workflow design_ (generate a patch, then a separate `workflow_run` workflow
     applies it). Same separation, but two files, and `workflow_run` workflows can only be tested
     after they're on `master`.
- **Rationale:** keeps the separation upstream uses, in one file that could be tested on a fork
  before merging.
- **Consequences:** _Easier:_ a broken or malicious test can't push anything but screenshots.
  _Harder:_ screenshots move between jobs as artifacts, and the PNG check runs in two places.

### Related issue(s)

Closes #153

### Tech Debt

**Introduced:**

- Two upstream workflow files are edited (`e2e-test.yml` trigger, `e2e-vrt-comment.yml` message and
  steps). They can conflict at upstream syncs; the edits are marked "Fork-only (issue #153)".
- After a bot commit, E2E runs twice: once started by the workflow, once when someone approves the
  held PR checks.
- Screenshots are made from the PR branch as it is, while PR checks test the branch merged with
  `master`. If `master` changed screenshots in the meantime they can differ; `STUDENTS.md` says to
  merge `master` first.
- An E2E run started by the workflow doesn't get a VRT Comment if it fails (the comment only runs
  for `pull_request` runs). The red check is still visible on the PR.
- The `.github/scripts` tests add a job (~1–2 min) to the Fork CI guard workflow.
- `package.json` / `yarn.lock`: `yaml` is now a root devDependency (one line each). The tests use it
  to read the workflow files. It was already installed through other packages at the same version,
  so nothing new is downloaded, but this is one more line that can conflict at upstream syncs.

**Encountered:**

- Upstream's `/update-vrt` workflows can't run here; replaced rather than adapted (issue Design).
- `budget.test.ts:466` ("switches to the mobile layout below the small breakpoint") failed in
  Functional shard 2 on the bot's commit in both E2E runs, but passed one commit earlier. The bot's
  commit only changed 3 PNGs, which Functional tests don't read (`toMatchThemeScreenshots` is a
  no-op without `VRT`). Not changed here; reported as #___ **[Liam: file the bug and fill in]**.
- Pre-existing shellcheck notes in `e2e-test.yml` / the comment's "Extract metadata" step left as is.

[TigerK9/actual-budget](https://github.com/TigerK9/actual-budget), not on this repository.

- **Why a fork:** GitHub only lets you start a `workflow_dispatch` workflow from the Actions tab
  once the workflow file is on the repository's **default branch**. Testing here would have meant
  merging untested code into our `master` first. The fork let me run the real workflow on GitHub
  without touching this repository.
- **Setup:** forked this repo, turned on Actions, pushed this PR's branch, and made it the fork's

No, you don't need it. And yes, removing it makes this check go away. Dependency Review only runs when a PR changes `yarn.lock`, so with no `yarn.lock` change it won't run on your PR at all.

Two things to know first:
- **The two files go together.** CI installs with `yarn --immutable`, which fails if `package.json` and `yarn.lock` disagree. Either both change or neither does.
- **Removing the line alone isn't enough.** The two test files `import { parse } from 'yaml'`, so they need a replacement.

## Two ways to remove it

| Option | What changes | Downside |
|---|---|---|
| **A. Tests read the YAML without a library** (recommended) | Swap `yaml` for a ~30-line helper in the tests that finds a step's `run: \|` script and the job's shell in our own workflow files. Revert `package.json` and `yarn.lock` to `master`'s. | A small hand-written parser. If the workflow's formatting changes in a way it doesn't handle, the tests **fail loudly** (an empty script can't pass), so they can't silently pass. |
| **B. Keep importing `yaml` without declaring it** | Only revert `package.json` and `yarn.lock`. | It only works because other packages happen to install `yaml`. If they stop, the tests break for reasons unrelated to them. I wouldn't do this. |

Either way, it's one new commit on the branch. PR #164 updates automatically, and the Tech Debt line about `yaml` comes out of the draft.

**One thing removing it doesn't fix:** Dependency Review is still broken for the whole repo. The next PR that touches `yarn.lock` will fail the same way. That's not yours to fix in #153, but tell the team, or whoever manages the repo settings, that **Dependency graph** needs to be enabled.

```mjs
// Test helper for the .github/scripts tests (issue #153): reads the parts of
// one of our workflow files that the tests run, without a YAML library.
//
// It understands only the layout our workflows use (2-space indents): top-level
// `env:` and `defaults:`, and under `jobs:` each job's `container:`,
// `defaults: run: shell:` and `steps:` (`- id/name/shell/run`). `run: |`
// blocks are returned like YAML's literal blocks: indentation removed, one
// trailing newline. Anything it doesn't understand is skipped, so a step it
// can't read comes back without a `run` and the tests that use it fail.
//
// Returns { env, defaults, jobs: { <id>: { container, defaults, steps } } }.

import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';

const KEY_VALUE = /^(\s*)(- )?([\w-]+):(?:\s+(.*))?$/;

function indentOf(line) {
  return line.length - line.trimStart().length;
}

// Plain, 'single-quoted' or "double-quoted" scalar (no escapes in ours
// except '' in single quotes)
function scalar(text) {
  const value = text.replace(/\s+#.*$/, '').trim();
  if (value.startsWith("'") && value.endsWith("'")) {
    return value.slice(1, -1).replaceAll("''", "'");
  }
  if (value.startsWith('"') && value.endsWith('"')) {
    return value.slice(1, -1);
  }
  return value;
}

// Reads the `|` block that starts after line `start`, for a key at `keyIndent`
function readBlock(lines, start, keyIndent) {
  const block = [];
  let i = start + 1;
  for (; i < lines.length; i++) {
    const line = lines[i];
    if (line.trim() !== '' && indentOf(line) <= keyIndent) {
      break;
    }
    block.push(line);
  }
  while (block.length > 0 && block.at(-1).trim() === '') {
    block.pop();
  }
  const blockIndent = Math.min(
    ...block.filter(line => line.trim() !== '').map(indentOf),
  );
  const text = block.map(line => line.slice(blockIndent)).join('\n');
  return { text: `${text}\n`, next: i };
}

export function readWorkflow(url) {
  const lines = readFileSync(url, 'utf8').split('\n');
  const workflow = { env: {}, defaults: {}, jobs: {} };
  let section = null; // top-level key we're in
  let job = null;
  let jobKey = null; // job-level key we're in (defaults, steps, ...)
  let step = null;

  for (let i = 0; i < lines.length; i++) {
    const line = lines[i];
    if (line.trim() === '' || line.trimStart().startsWith('#')) {
      continue;
    }
    const match = line.match(KEY_VALUE);
    if (!match) {
      continue;
    }
    const [, spaces, dash, key, value = ''] = match;
    const indent = spaces.length;

    if (indent === 0) {
      section = key;
      continue;
    }

    if (section === 'env' && indent === 2) {
      workflow.env[key] = scalar(value);
    } else if (section === 'defaults' && key === 'shell') {
      workflow.defaults.run = { shell: scalar(value) };
    } else if (section === 'jobs' && indent === 2) {
      job = { container: undefined, defaults: {}, steps: [] };
      workflow.jobs[key] = job;
      jobKey = null;
    } else if (section === 'jobs' && job && indent === 4) {
      jobKey = key;
      if (key === 'container') {
        job.container = value === '' ? {} : scalar(value);
      }
    } else if (jobKey === 'defaults' && key === 'shell') {
      job.defaults.run = { shell: scalar(value) };
    } else if (jobKey === 'steps' && indent === 6 && dash) {
      step = {};
      job.steps.push(step);
      setStepKey(step, key, value, lines, i, indent + 2);
    } else if (jobKey === 'steps' && step && indent === 8 && !dash) {
      const next = setStepKey(step, key, value, lines, i, indent);
      if (next !== undefined) {
        i = next - 1;
      }
    }
  }
  return workflow;
}

// Sets one of a step's keys; returns the next line to read after a `|` block
function setStepKey(step, key, value, lines, index, keyIndent) {
  if (!['id', 'name', 'shell', 'run'].includes(key)) {
    return undefined;
  }
  if (key === 'run' && value.trim() === '|') {
    const { text, next } = readBlock(lines, index, keyIndent);
    step.run = text;
    return next;
  }
  step[key] = scalar(value);
  return undefined;
}
